CIX. In nomine domini amen. Cum jam dudum inter prouidos viros religiosos, videlicet fralres frai rem Henricum abbatem ac conuentum sui monasterii Altiuadensis ordinis Cisterciensis, ex parte vna et discretum ¡virum dominum Mauricium plebanum et rectorem ligitti- mum ecclesie in Stropnycz ipsius ecclesie nomine parte ex altera grauis esset confrouersia exorta super jure percipiendi decimas agrorum et prediorum omnium parochianorum ecclesie prefate in Stropnycz, prenominato domino abbafe ac conuentu suprascripti monasterii ac ordinis priuilegia de percepcione omnium decimarum tocius parrochie antedicte producentibus et allegantibus, se fuisse esse et fuisse in pacifica quasi possessione inris percipiendi easdem decimas a tempore, cuius contrarii memoria non existit; ipso autem domino Mauricio rectore predicte ecclesie jus pro se et ecclesie commune allegante et dicente, predictas decimas eidem deberi sue ecclesie nomine utpote sitas infra limites ecclesie prelibate. Tandem cum di u in iudicio et extra et connu conseruatoribus iurum et priui- legiorum a sede apostolica monasterio prenotato concessis litigassent, pro bona pacis et concordie ac amicabilis composicionis in nos Pe- trum de Rosenberch prepositum ecclesie omnium sanctorum in castro Pragensi et canonicum ecclesie Pragensis sponte et beniuole ex utraque parte laboribus et litis expensis parcere cupientes compro 119 mittere curauerunt, se sub pena per nos in pronunciacione appen- ilenda obligantes. Ac deinde termino pro pronunciacione ac amicabili eomposicione facienda adueniente prefixo nos dei nomine inuocato in parcium presencia personali ac earundem iuribus et allegacionibus intellects talem inter suprascriptas partes laudacionem pronunciacio- nem ac amicabilem composicionem fecimus, vt scilicet prenominatus abbas et eius conuentus nomine monasterii prelibatarum decimarum possessores jure percipiendi prefatas decimas utantur libere et fru- antur, quemadmodum eas sine cuiusquam inpedimento consueuerunt percipere a tempore, cuius contrarii memoria non existit. Ne tamen ecclesia sepefata in Stropnycz omnino decimis, que sunt tributa egencium animarum fraudaretur, necnon penitus orbaretur, laudamus ordinamus et amicabiliter componentes statuimus arbitrando, vt se- pedictus abbas vniuersos arabiles laneos eiusdem parrochie in Stro- pniycz secundum mensuram et quantitatem Paczouiensium laneorum faciat mensurare, et quotquot de agris solummodo arabilibus cultibi- libus seu seminabilibus tempore mensuracionis inventis laneos ibidem in tota parrochia Paczouiensis quantitatis reperiet, tot mensuras in opido ipso Stropnycz consuetas de grano siliginis vnam videlicet mensuram necnon et auene de quolibet laneo vnam mensuram prefato plebano nomine ecclesie sue tribuat singulis annis perpetuis tempo- ribus persoluat. De curiis autem seu allodiis mobilium tune temporis cxislentibus, de quibus eciam predictus abbas nomine sui monasterii decimas inconcusse consueuit per longissima retroacta tempora per cipere, de curia videlicet domini Johannis, qui Sprinczel dicitur, item de curia domini Luduici de Czeuetlaren, item Stephani de Crophslog, item de curia in Piberslog Nycolaii Sagitarii, item Leulini in Gedlicz, item de curia Hogerii in Seyben, item Johannis in Gutenprun, infra limites ipsius ecclesie volumus et arbitratoria auctoritate mandamus decimas vniuersas, cum collecte fuerint, per medium diuidendas, me- dietatemque earundem decimarum dicti abbas et conuentus nomine monasterii percipiant, alteramque medietatem plebanus recolligat memoratus. Insuper pronunciamus statuentes, ut quecunque parcium ipsarum a prescripta nostra pronunciacione resiliret ac eidem parere contempneret, alteri parti composicionemobseruare volenti quindecim sexagenas grossorum denariorum Pragensium assignaret pro pena et alias quindecim sexagenas eiusdem monete ad fabricam Pragensis ecclesie dare deberet certis super pene solucione ab alterutra parto 120 fideiussoribus constitutis. Ego Kathenna relicta oliim Vlrici dicti Schauffler de Seherleins ad vniuersorum notitiam volo peruenire tenore presencium publice protestans, quod ego animo deliberato et sano meorum liberorum ex me per ipsum Vlricum prorreatorum et amicorum ipsorum ad hoc accedente consensu pariter et assensu honorabilius et religiosis viris dominis Henrico abbati totique conuentui monasterii in Altovado ordinis Cysterciensis Pragensis diocesis ad officium pitancie dedi donaui resignaui libere et absolute rite et racionabiliter totaliter et omnino perpetue tenendum possidendum alienandum vendendum iure perhenni cum omnibus censibus iuribus consuetudmibus robotariis ipsum molendinum in predicte villa situm, in quo molendinator no mine proprio Leo longam et diutinam personalem fecit residenciam, in quo molendinoipse abbas et conuentus prefati cenobii singulis annis habuerunt et a nobis receperunt per meum antedictum maritum pie memorie Vlricum et per me et meos heredes censum firmum et cer 121 tum ipsis porrectum triginta tantum denarios Patauienses, quem cen- sum ipsi progenitores mariti mei suprascripti dederunt in remedium animarum su;rrum ipso dicto monasterio in Altovado; quod molen- dinum totum cum fundo per omnia, ut supra dictum est, ego Kathe- rina prescripta cum vniuersis meis heredibus plenarie contradidi sepefato cenobio ob remedium et salutem iamdicti et prescripti mariti et omnium suorum ac meorum predecessorum, totum ius, quod mich i et dictis meis liberis in dicto molendino competebat sev competere posset quouis modo in futuro, in supradictos dominos abbatem et co- nuentum transfero et transfundo hereditario pacifice et quiete. IQ cuius rei euidens testimonium presens scriptum et priuilegium preno- minato monasterio et conuentui in Altovado presentaui et conscribi feci cum appensione sigillorum domini Marchardi militis strennui de Parisching protunc castellani caslri in Rosenberch, et honorabilis viri Zmilonis de Ruben, qui ambo de certa ipsoram sciencia ob mul- tarum mearum precum deuntam et incessabilem instanciam sua sigilla presentibus appenderunt in testimonium et robur omnium suprascrip- torum, ipsis tamen iam dictis viris sine omni dampno et preiudicio semper et vbique quolibet postposito et semoto. entries.english:
1360, 31 December, Krumau. Peter von Rosenberg, provost of the Church of All Saints at Prague Castle, settles the dispute that arose over the parish tithes of Strobnitz between Abbot Heinrich of Hohenfurt and his convent on one side and the parish priest Mauritz of Strobnitz on the other.

1360, undated. Katherina, widow of Ulrich called Schauffler of Sacheries, gives the mill belonging to her in the village of Sacheries to Abbot Heinrich and the convent of Hohenfurt for the salvation of her husband's soul.

CIX. In the name of the Lord, amen. Since a serious dispute had long existed between the prudent religious men, namely Brother Heinrich, abbot, and the convent of his monastery of Hohenfurt of the Cistercian order on one side, and the discerning man Lord Mauritz, parish priest and lawful rector of the church at Strobnitz, on behalf of that church on the other, concerning the right to collect tithes from the fields and properties of all parishioners of that church at Strobnitz: the said abbot and convent produced and cited the privileges of the monastery concerning collection of all tithes throughout the parish, alleging that they had been and remained in peaceful possession of the right to collect them from time immemorial; while Lord Mauritz, rector of that church, claimed the right for himself and the common church, saying that the tithes were owed to his church because they lay within its boundaries. After they had litigated for a long time, in court and out of court, before the conservators of the rights and privileges granted by the Apostolic See to the aforesaid monastery, both parties, wishing of their own free will to spare themselves the labor and expense of litigation for the sake of peace, concord, and an amicable settlement, agreed to submit the matter to us, Peter von Rosenberg, provost of the Church of All Saints at Prague Castle and canon of Prague Church, binding themselves under a penalty to be set by our decision. When the appointed date for our decision and amicable settlement arrived, after invoking God's name and hearing the parties and their respective rights and arguments in their presence, we made the following award, decision, and amicable settlement: the aforesaid abbot and his convent, on behalf of the monastery, shall freely use and enjoy the right to collect the aforesaid tithes, as they have customarily collected them without anyone's hindrance from time immemorial. Yet, so that the said church at Strobnitz should not be wholly deprived of tithes, which are sustenance for needy souls, nor entirely stripped of them, we award, order, and amicably settle as follows. The said abbot shall have all arable hides in that parish at Strobnitz measured according to the measure and size of the hides at Paczow. For each hide's worth of cultivated or cultivable arable land found at the time of measurement throughout the parish, he shall give and pay to the aforesaid parish priest, on behalf of his church, one measure of rye grain and one measure of oats, in the customary measures of the town of Strobnitz, every year in perpetuity. As for the courts or manors then existing, from which the aforesaid abbot on behalf of his monastery had also customarily collected tithes without interruption for a very long time—namely the court of Lord Johann called Sprinczel; the court of Lord Luduicus of Czeuetlaren; that of Stephan of Crophslog; the court at Piberslog of Nycolaus Sagitarius; that of Leulin at Gedlicz; the court of Hogerius at Seyben; and that of Johann at Gutenprun—lying within the boundaries of that church, by our arbitral authority we order that all tithes, when collected, be divided equally: the said abbot and convent on behalf of the monastery shall receive one half, and the aforesaid parish priest shall collect the other half. We further decree that whichever party withdraws from this decision and refuses to comply shall pay the party willing to observe the settlement fifteen sexagenae of Prague groschen as a penalty, and another fifteen sexagenae of the same currency to the fabric of Prague Church; sureties for payment of the penalty have been provided by each party. This was done in our castle at Krumau before suitable witnesses: Lord Bochdancius, dean of Dudleben; Wenceslaus, parish priest of Blanitz; and Dyrslaus, parish priest of Krems, specially invited for this purpose, in the personal presence of the parties. In testimony of this, I ordered these letters to be made and secured them with the attachment of my seal, the seal of the aforesaid Mauritz, parish priest of Strobnitz, and those of the aforesaid witnesses. Given at the place aforesaid, in the year of the Lord 1360, on the last day of December.

Six seals hang from parchment strips, fairly well preserved but poorly impressed. (The following descriptions identify the seals.)

CX. 1360, undated. I, Katherina, widow of the late Ulrich called Schauffler of Sacheries, make known publicly to all by these presents that, with deliberate judgment and the consent and approval of my children by that Ulrich and of their friends, I have given, donated, and freely and absolutely surrendered, lawfully and reasonably, in perpetuity, to the honorable and religious men Lords Heinrich, abbot, and the entire convent of the monastery of Hohenfurt of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Prague, for the almonry, the mill situated in the aforesaid village, where the miller Leo by name has long resided in person. In that mill, the said abbot and convent have each year received from my aforesaid husband, of pious memory, and from me and my heirs, a fixed and certain rent of thirty Passau denarii, which the ancestors of my aforesaid husband gave to the monastery of Hohenfurt for the remedy of their souls. The whole mill, with its land, as stated above, I, the aforesaid Katherina, together with all my heirs, have fully transferred to the aforesaid monastery for the remedy and salvation of the soul of my aforesaid husband and of all his and my predecessors; I transfer and convey hereditarily, peacefully and quietly, to the aforesaid abbot and convent all the right that belonged or might in any way belong to me and my said children in the mill. In clear testimony of this, I presented this written instrument and privilege to the aforesaid monastery and convent and caused it to be drawn up with the attachment of the seals of Lord Marchard, a vigorous knight of Parisching, then castellan of Rosenberg Castle, and the honorable Zmilo of Ruben. Both, in full knowledge of the matter and at my many urgent entreaties, attached their seals to these presents as testimony and confirmation of all the foregoing, without any damage or prejudice to the said men, always and everywhere. Given and done in the year of the Lord 1360. Two small seals hang from parchment strips in green wax.
